text:
cust-support: FYI - customer (ACME Analytics) started seeing a big spike of 502/timeout errors hitting hosted inference in eu-west-1 right after our scheduled cert sync window. They see TLS handshake timeouts and sometimes DNS resolution failures. Request path: POST /v1/generate -> gateway -> custapi -> model-pool.

maya: Can you paste the customer's example request id and a short curl repro? We should collect logs + tcpdump.

cust-support: request id: r-0a1b2c3d4e, tstamp 2024-06-22T09:12:43Z. Customer sent a small repro: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":32}' \\n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
They see multiple attempts and final error : "TLS handshake timeout" or sometimes "DNS lookup timed out" in the client library.

deploy-bot: Noted scheduled cert-sync completed at 2024-06-22T09:10:00Z across regions. No automatic rollback triggered.

sam: Thanks — quick hypotheses: 1) intermediate cert chain propagation lag to some edge hosts, 2) resolver returning SERVFAIL/timeout due to EDNS0/UDP truncation, 3) a subset of hosts temporarily blackholing TLS after reload due to race in SNI mapping.

eli: I pulled gateway logs for r-0a1b2c3d4e: upstream connection attempts show repeated connect() timeouts to custapi backend IPs, then ECONNRESET. Gateway TLSDebug shows handshake started -> no response. Snippet: 
```
[09:12:43] connect to 10.34.12.87:443 attempt 1 -> timeout
[09:12:44] TLS handshake init, SNI="api.redwood.ai"
[09:12:44] TLS handshake timeout after 5s
[09:12:45] upstream fallback to alternate pool -> connect ok
```

maya: Interesting that alternate pool worked. Did customer see intermittent success?

cust-support: They said 4/5 requests failed for ~7 minutes then traffic recovered. They can reproduce if they hammer during that window.

sam: Can we check resolver metrics at that time? If DNS timeouts align then resolv path is suspect. Also check if any nodes had a stale certchain or missing intermediate.

eli: Resolver metrics show a spike in query latency to 8s from eu-resolver cluster at 09:12:40, with ~12% UDP truncation rate then increased TCP fallbacks. Also one EC2 instance in eu-gw-1 reported high CPU and many threads blocked during cert load at 09:10–09:14.

nicole: Customer impact note: they use a short client retry backoff which amplifies the errors into visible 502s. They're asking for an RCA and mitigation so it doesn't happen during future cert syncs.

maya: Immediate mitigation options: 1) Rollforward cert sync to ensure all hosts get full chain + restart staging sequence with warm handoff, 2) temporarily route that customer's traffic to the alternate pool which had success, 3) increase DNS TCP fallback and lower UDP use in eu-resolver if EDNS0 issues. Need eng sign-off.

sam: For root cause candidate: cert reload triggers blocking work that competes with resolver threads on some gateway VMs -> TLS accept/connect stalls -> client retries cause upstream 502s. The UDP truncation suggests our resolvers were getting larger responses (OCSP/CAA?) and hitting MTU/EDNS0 issues. Combined, this gives a window where both DNS and TLS were degraded.

eli: Action items I'm running: collect pcap from eu-gw-1 during window (asked SRE for pcap), extract cert chains from any hosts that failed to present full chain, correlate kernel logs for OOM/lock contention on cert reload.

maya: Also please capture customer-side SPDY/TCP traces if they can (or at least their curl -v output). Ask them to set env "RES_OPTIONS="timeout:1 attempts:5 rotate" temporarily? Maybe suggest they switch to resolver 8.8.8.8 for repro to confirm resolver involvement.

cust-support: Customer provided additional curl output showing DNS timeout followed by manual retry success: 
```
*   Trying 54.239.11.21:443...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* connect to 54.239.11.21 port 443 failed: Operation timed out
* Closing connection 0
* DNS lookup timed out; trying next server
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (3.124.99.11) port 443
* TLS handshake completed
> HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

sam: That lines up. Root cause = transient resolver failures + a small subset of gateways with blocking cert reload. Long-term fixes: make cert reload non-blocking (hot-swap without pausing worker threads), improve resolver MTU/EDNS handling (force TCP for large RRsets), and add canary window that routes traffic off nodes during cert reload.

eli: Short term: route ACME Analytics to alternate pool (maya/sales can approve) + schedule an out-of-band cert reload health-check next sync. Also rollout a quick guard: if cert reload causes >2s pause, mark node as draining.

maya: I'll coordinate routing and customer comms. Sam/eli, please add a postmortem section with root cause, timeline, and the three mitigation PRs.

deploy-bot: Incident ticket INC-2024-482 created and linked to this thread.

cust-support: Customer happy with routing fix for now; asked for ETA on code change to make reload non-blocking.

sam: Rough ETA for a minimal non-blocking reload is ~2 weeks, will prepare a scoped PR for review.

eli: I will upload collected pcap + cert artifacts to the incident ticket once SRE share is available.

maya: Thanks everyone. Follow-ups: PRs, postmortem, customer update in 48h. :thumbsup:
